children: Novartis's latest clinical-trial setback raises questions about the Swiss drugmaker's acquisition track record and leaves a sales hole to be plugged in the early 2030s, Deutsche Bank's Emmanuel Papadakis says in a research note. News that drug candidate del-desiran missed the target of a late-stage study in rare neuromuscular disorder known as myotonic dystrophy type 1 came shortly after cardiovascular drug pelacarsen failed another trial. Del-desiran was the first proof point for the recent $12 billion Avidity acquisition, the analyst says. Moreover, it leaves a hole to be addressed in the early 2030s when big drugs like Cosentyx, Kisqali and Kesimpta lose patent protection, he adds. Deutsche Bank cuts its recommendation on Novartis stock to hold from buy and trims its target price to 120 Swiss francs from 140 francs. Shares fall 0.8% to 110.86 francs. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
